budget.note: Overnight program (Martin, 2026-09-26): 8-hour window; 25 more worker runs and 2 more Opus reviews on top of the pilot's usage.

settled: Representation core = 1-DoF primitives {fixed, revolute, continuous, prismatic}; no helical; floating/planar/ball refused (UnsupportedConstruct), not expanded.
URDF frame convention: joint origin in parent frame, child frame = joint frame at q=0, axis through origin; xyz/rpy stored verbatim as parsed.
Pilot couplings: AffineCoupling only (URDF mimic). Limits stored verbatim on primitives; admissible box derived; conflicts reported (LimitConflict), never clipped.
Tolerances frozen in hand_sampler/grammar_bench/tolerances.py (1e-12 analytic, 1e-10 oracle).
Benchmark lives in hand_sampler/grammar_bench (separate package, separate commits); implementation in hand_sampler/grammar.
Coverage = expressible / in-support inventory, not parse-back derivability (deferred to M2 as constructive reconstruction).
No ContinuumSegment node; Approximation annotations instead; PCC macro deferred to M3.
Oracle references are frozen JSON generated by refgen scripts run in the conda env 'piper' (Pinocchio 3.4.0, MuJoCo 3.2.3); tests run on system Python 3.10.
Purpose: the representation is the substrate for evolution over a grammar, not an importer of real hands. Real hands are in-support/expressiveness checks only; exact matching is not a goal.

Palm-ness is a per-body flag; the palm set is a connected subtree containing the root; a palm joint is an ordinary joint whose child is a palm body. Any number of palm articulation directions; nothing anthropomorphic is assumed.

Palm geometry: convex hull of all palm bodies' capsules at q=0, cut into one convex cell per palm body by a plane through each palm joint origin that contains the joint axis with normal n = d - (d.a)a (d = direction from parent palm joint/root to this joint). Fingers use capsules. Validator: every cell has positive volume; finger mounts lie on their palm body's cell. No geometry genes; mass from cell/capsule volume and one density.
Closed-chain solver deferred to 'only if a production needs it'; the LoopClosure placeholder stays.
Iteration-3 grammar productions: root, palm bodies with optional palm joint (tighter travel than finger joints), finger chains of phalanx capsules, optional intra-finger affine coupling.
Every generated hand has at least one palm body (Martin, 2026-09-25). Import-from-URDF only needs to work; it is not a priority.

Palm cut plane refinement (coordinator, 2026-09-26, to confirm with Martin): plane through the palm joint origin containing its axis, normal = perp_axis(d_child - d_parent) where d_parent is the parent's segment direction toward its tip; sibling overlaps resolved by nearest spine; cells sharing a cut face are adjacent (collision-filtered).

Palm cells (2026-09-26, coordinator after worker counterexample): the plane-carved partition cannot hold for entangled palm trees (seed 10: three palm bodies whose own planes are non-discriminating; no single plane conserves volume and keeps both spines). Replaced by nearest-spine assignment of hull samples, one convex hull per palm body, overlaps allowed only between pairs recorded as adjacent (collision-filtered); coverage and containment asserted, exact partition not claimed. To confirm with Martin.

issues.hypothesis: A 1-DoF-primitive kinematic graph with verbatim URDF poses and affine couplings reproduces Pinocchio FK on Allegro/LEAP/Barrett at 1e-10 and sympy closed forms at 1e-12.
issues.evidence: commits 5bf270d (benchmark) + e87e887 (implementation); 13 passed; max err 2.0e-16 m / 5.3e-16 rad vs Pinocchio, 2.6e-17 / 3.6e-16 vs sympy

issues.hypothesis: hand_root cut silently drops a coupling whose source lies above the cut (adapters/urdf.py:194); should be a LossReport entry. No dev hand is affected yet (SHARPA has no mimic).
issues.evidence: LossReport.couplings_cut, tested with a synthetic cut; commit 82e46e0

issues.hypothesis: Extremal 'zero' configuration is omitted when 0 is outside the admissible box (Allegro, Barrett -> 70 configs, LEAP -> 71). Acceptable; document in tolerances/refgen rather than forcing 71.
Exact JSON round trip and a URDF exporter that re-emits verbatim poses and mimic tags reproduce the frozen Pinocchio references on the exported files; SHARPA imports with hand_root=left_hand_C_MC.
issues.evidence: commits dfdb04b+82e46e0; 45 passed; export-oracle 0.0 on Allegro/LEAP/Barrett, 4.5e-16 on SHARPA; Ability 1120 poses 5.7e-17, Inspire 1330 poses 1.2e-16

issues.hypothesis: A typed grammar (root, palm bodies with optional palm joints, digit chains with branching and affine couplings, separate parameter table) with replayable derivations generates only valid models whose exported URDFs Pinocchio agrees with at 1e-10, and its support covers the listed constructs.
issues.evidence: commits 403e3cb+acf57e5; 754 passed; oracle 66,476 poses 3.9e-16; but coordinator probe over 300 seeds: 0 in-digit branches, 0 palm trees; audit key 'branch' mislabels

issues.hypothesis: Mounting branch digits on the branching phalanx body and parenting palm bodies to any existing palm body yields real in-digit branching and palm trees, measured directly by the audit, without breaking replay/vary/oracle agreement.
issues.evidence: commits ab37531+901a0ce; coordinator probe 300 seeds: 220 in-digit branches, 109 palm trees; 755 passed; oracle 84,613 poses 7.4e-16

issues.hypothesis: Counting digits structurally for imported hands (root children / leaf chains) removes the vacuous digit_count_out_of_range:0 item and leaves the honest grid/limit findings.
issues.evidence: commits 6b7387b+8b86062+49b886e; 813 passed; no digit_count_out_of_range items; ORCA counts as 1 digit (wrist-gated), noted

issues.hypothesis: Geometry data model: mount points off host segment (derive.py:235), inconsistent palm segment (derive.py:215/227), palm_body_count=0 leaves no palm geometry. Must be fixed before the hull step.
issues.evidence: commits 565854c+dca4d7a; probe 300 hands: 0 off-segment, 0 rootless; 2314 passed; oracle 88,484 poses 5.1e-16

issues.hypothesis: Coverage 'expressible' is near-vacuous and two audit keys are mislabelled (nonperpendicular_axis, two_nonparallel_palm_joints); ORCA children-per-body not checked.
Couplings ignore source joint type; no derivation validator; vary keeps parent seed; rules.py types unused; test hygiene items (local tolerances, approx, body-set asserts, unused analytic refs).

Real fingers have mid-chain frame rotations/lateral offsets (continuation_pose) that the straight-rod digit convention cannot express; a 'rest bend' production (continuation rpy and lateral offset on a phalanx) would extend support. Decide with Martin whether evolution needs it.
issues.evidence: pilot-report: 9/10 real hands fail only/mainly on continuation_pose

issues.hypothesis: Bisector cutting plane (through the joint, containing the axis, bisecting parent and child spines) plus nearest-spine sibling resolution yields positive-volume cells that contain their digit mounts; cells sharing a cut face are recorded as adjacent for collision filtering.
issues.evidence: 200 seeds: 0 mounts/spines outside, min cell 5e-6 m3, overlap 7.4%, 2834 passed in 377 s; routine test now 40 seeds

issues.hypothesis: No operator adds/removes a palm body or toggles a palm joint; add_digit/remove_digit change ~7 joints because new digits are sampled at full size. Evolution needs minimal structural operators (add 1-phalanx digit, add/remove palm body, toggle palm joint).

next_action: E3 running: minimal structural operators + reachability hill-climb to 4 targets; E4 redundancy counts.
